scope: Exploratory CPU, hybrid WebGPU and browser SVG presentation on a shared desktop; not the release performance gate
order: Rotating and reversing CPU, GPU, SVG sample order
correctness: Every CPU/hybrid sample is byte-identical to the CPU reference. SVG export bytes must repeat exactly; browser SVG pixel variation and accuracy ranges are reported without a conformance or deterministic-pixel claim.
render_time: CPU and hybrid build fresh pixels, including hybrid program/upload/completion/readback. SVG reuses one page export, its embedded image resources and decoded browser image, then performs fresh Canvas rasterization/readback.
frame_time: CPU/hybrid render including worker/WASI transport; retained SVG performs no worker export request after setup.
excluded_once: first GPU buffer allocation and packet validation
initial SVG export and embedded-image conversion
initial SVG validation, parse, image decode and first readback
required_separate_reporting: initial SVG setup and host cache hit
interactive_demo: Nine samples after two warmups; illustrative only
svg_slow_case_policy: An initial completed SVG raster exceeding 250 ms caps SVG at 3 timed samples and 1 warmup; CPU/hybrid keep the requested count. Actual counts and cap are reported. No slow input is silently excluded.
presentation: 12 samples after 2 warmups in top and centre 480px viewports. CPU/hybrid rebuild pixels; SVG reuses its exported page and decoded image. No forced full-page SVG readback. Request to two animation-frame opportunities, not scanout.
zoom: 18 fresh-resolution samples after 3 warmups across 1x, 1.5x and 2x, alternating top/centre viewport. SVG retains its vector image. A 60-frame CSS gesture uses the centre viewport. A path stops after a frame above 250 ms once at least 3 samples are collected, preserving earlier samples. A slow gesture stops after at least 3 frames. Actual counts are reported. Untimed accuracy readback samples the retained image and also compares it with fresh SVG serialization.
svg_cache_scope: One host export per current recorded page, reset on page/document change, bounded by 64 MiB. Encoded images are deduplicated inside that artifact. One parsed/decoded browser artifact per comparison, shared by all its samples. No application raster pixel cache.
